issues.evidence: 5 out of 5 pages are missing structured data (JSON-LD schema).
issues.problem: Search engines and AI algorithms cannot programmatically read entity relationships, author details, or product details.
issues.whyItMatters: Structured schema (like Organization, Person, Product, Breadcrumbs) clarifies entities and establishes direct knowledge-graph connections.
issues.recommendation: Add structured JSON-LD data to pages. Add Organization and Person (Yogi Manu) schema on the homepage, Product schema on the Shop page, and Service schema on /onsite and /tarot.
issues.implementation: Embed metadata scripts of type "application/ld+json" within Next.js page components.

issues.evidence: Pages (/, /onsite, /retreats, /tarot) are marked "use client", causing them to render on the client side.
issues.problem: Search bots and lightweight AI crawlers might fail to render client-side Javascript, missing the main copy of the page.
issues.whyItMatters: If crawlers cannot render JS properly, they cannot index the text content required to match query entities.
issues.recommendation: Minimize the use of client-rendered components. Move state logic into dedicated leaf components and leave parent pages as Server Components.
issues.implementation: Refactor pages so the page.tsx is a Server Component, importing Client Components only for interactive sections like forms.

issues.evidence: Images with generic filenames (like 'generic.jpg') found on: / (2 images), /tarot (1 images).
issues.problem: Image search and AI retrieval algorithms cannot verify the context of the image file path.
issues.whyItMatters: Search engines leverage filename semantics to map image search indexes. Generic filenames are less authoritative.
issues.recommendation: Rename images to reflect their semantic context (e.g., kirtan-meditation-session.jpg) instead of placeholder names.
issues.implementation: Rename files in the public/images directory and update their imports/references in code.

issues.evidence: Product items are represented as single cards without a structured comparison matrix or specifications list.
issues.problem: It is difficult for structured AI engines to pull comparisons (e.g., pros/cons, weight, price) of yoga products.
issues.whyItMatters: AI systems frequently pull comparisons to answer prompts like "Manduka vs cork yoga blocks". Tabular data simplifies passage extraction.
issues.recommendation: Add a structured product comparison or recommendation guide table comparing key tools.
issues.implementation: Create a responsive comparison Table in ShopSection.tsx comparing dimensions, materials, and price tiers.

issues.evidence: Inconsistent branding and category naming: referred to as "Yoga, Kirtan & Spiritual Teachings" on home title, "wellness programs" on onsite, and "curated recommendations" on shop.
issues.problem: Entity relationships are not clearly structured. AI models cannot synthesize a single, concise description of Yogi Manu's services.
issues.whyItMatters: Consistent category descriptions across LinkedIn, socials, and on-site files allow AI systems to confidently map the entity description.
issues.recommendation: Standardize the primary organization bio: "Yogi Manu is a spiritual teacher and wellness program provider specialized in classical yoga, kirtan, and tarot." and apply this description across pages.
issues.implementation: Update metadata descriptions and About copy to ensure semantic alignment.

issues.evidence: No analytics tracking configuration (GSC API, Bing Webmaster tools integration, custom search parameters) found in source.
issues.problem: No ability to monitor brand referrals from ChatGPT, Perplexity, or Copilot.
issues.whyItMatters: Without measurement, you cannot determine which keywords or content updates are successfully driving generative AI visibility.
issues.recommendation: Set up UTM tracking and custom hostname filters to isolate ChatGPT Search and Perplexity referral sessions in analytics.
issues.implementation: Implement a basic analytics hook in layout.tsx or configure search query parameter checks.
